output.title: Why UK Mums Switch Infant Formula Brands
output.audience: Mothers in the UK aged 25 to 40 who use or have used infant formula
topics: Current formula use and how the first brand was chosen
Triggers and reasons for switching formula brands
The switching decision process and information sources
Influences such as health professionals, family, friends and online communities
Price, availability and practical factors
Baby's response and feelings about switching
Future intentions and what would make them stay or switch again

questions.text: To start, could you tell me a bit about your little one and how formula fits into your feeding routine at the moment?
questions.goal: Build rapport and understand the respondent's current feeding situation and how central formula is to it.

questions.text: Thinking back to when you first started using formula, how did you end up with the brand you chose?
questions.goal: Understand how the initial brand choice was made and what shaped it.

questions.text: Can you walk me through the time or times you've changed formula brands, from when you first started thinking about it to when you made the change?
questions.goal: Map the switching journey and identify the triggers that started it.

questions.text: What were the main reasons behind your decision to switch?
questions.goal: Uncover the core motivations for switching, in the respondent's own words.

questions.text: Who or what, if anyone, did you turn to for advice or information when deciding which formula to move to?
questions.goal: Identify the people, professionals and sources that influence the choice of a new brand.

questions.text: How, if at all, did things like price, offers or being able to find it in the shops play a part in your decision?
questions.goal: Understand the role of cost, promotions and availability in switching.

questions.text: How did your baby get on after the switch?
questions.goal: Learn how the baby's reaction shaped the respondent's view of whether the switch worked.

questions.text: How did you feel, as a parent, about making the change?
questions.goal: Explore the emotions involved in switching, such as confidence, worry or relief, without assuming any particular feeling.

questions.text: Looking ahead, what would make you stick with the formula you use now, and what might lead you to change again?
questions.goal: Understand future loyalty drivers and potential triggers for further switching.

output.title: Shopper Reactions to the New Plant-Based Packaging
output.audience: Adults aged 30 to 55 who do a weekly grocery shop
topics: Weekly grocery shopping habits
Role of packaging in product choice
Understanding of plant-based packaging
Reactions to the new plant-based packaging
Influence of the packaging on likelihood to buy
Hesitations or concerns about the packaging
Future expectations for grocery packaging

questions.text: Could you walk me through how your weekly grocery shop usually goes, from planning it to getting it home?
questions.goal: Understand the respondent's shopping routine and context before discussing packaging.

questions.text: When you're standing in front of a few similar products on the shelf, how do you decide which one goes in your basket?
questions.goal: Learn which factors drive product choice, unprompted, before packaging is mentioned.

questions.text: What part, if any, does the packaging play when you're choosing what to buy?
questions.goal: Gauge how much weight packaging carries in purchase decisions relative to other factors.

questions.text: When you hear the phrase 'plant-based packaging', what comes to mind?
questions.goal: Uncover the respondent's understanding, associations and any misconceptions about plant-based packaging.

questions.text: Looking at the new packaging we've shown you, how do you feel about it?
questions.goal: Capture honest, unprompted reactions to the new packaging, whether positive, negative or neutral.

questions.text: How, if at all, would this packaging change whether you'd buy the product?
questions.goal: Test whether and how the new packaging influences likelihood to buy, without assuming a positive effect.

questions.text: What, if anything, would make you hesitate before buying a product in this packaging?
questions.goal: Identify any barriers such as price, durability, trust in claims or appearance.

questions.text: What would you want to know about this packaging before deciding how you feel about it?
questions.goal: Find out what information or proof shoppers need to evaluate the packaging and its claims.

questions.text: Looking ahead, how do you see packaging fitting into the way you choose your groceries over the next few years?
questions.goal: Understand future expectations and whether packaging is likely to grow or shrink as a factor in choice.

comments.questions_non_leading: Q7: It presumes the respondent has a usual app and has switched away from it.

output.title: Weeknight Food Delivery App Choice Among People in Their Twenties
output.audience: People in their twenties who order food through delivery apps on weeknights
topics: How the app is chosen on a weeknight
Price
Delivery speed
Choice of restaurants
Loyalty schemes

questions.text: Tell me about the last time you ordered food through an app on a weeknight. What was going on, and how did it play out from start to finish?
questions.goal: To get a concrete, recent story that sets the scene and shows the natural decision process without prompting.

questions.text: When you decide to order in on a weeknight, how do you pick which app to open first?
questions.goal: To understand the habits, defaults and triggers that drive which app gets opened before any specific factor is raised.

questions.text: How, if at all, does the total cost of an order, including fees, affect which app you end up using?
questions.goal: To learn how much weight price and fees carry in app choice and how people compare costs across apps.

questions.text: How does the delivery time an app shows you factor into your decision, if it does at all?
questions.goal: To understand how important delivery speed is on weeknights and how much people trust the estimated times.

questions.text: How would you describe the range of restaurants on the apps you use, and what role does that play in where you order from?
questions.goal: To find out how restaurant choice and availability of specific favourites shape app selection.

questions.text: What experience, if any, have you had with rewards, memberships or points schemes on delivery apps?
questions.goal: To learn whether and how loyalty schemes and subscriptions influence which app people return to.

questions.text: Think of a time you switched from your usual app to a different one. What led to that?
questions.goal: To uncover the factors strong enough to break habits and how price, speed, choice and rewards trade off in practice.

questions.text: Looking ahead, what would an app need to change or offer for you to use it more often on weeknights?
questions.goal: To capture forward-looking needs and unmet expectations that could inform product and marketing decisions.

output.title: Why New Gym Members Cancel Within Their First Three Months
output.audience: Gym members aged 18 to 45 who cancelled their membership this year within their first three months
topics: Reasons for joining the gym
Expectations before joining
Early experiences at the gym
How gym visits fit into daily life
Moments that led to the decision to cancel
The cancellation process
What might have changed the outcome
Future plans for exercise and gyms

questions.text: To start, could you tell me a bit about how exercise or staying active fits into your life these days?
questions.goal: To build rapport and understand the respondent's general relationship with exercise as context for their gym experience.

questions.text: Thinking back to when you signed up, what was going on in your life that made you decide to join a gym?
questions.goal: To learn the motivations and life circumstances that triggered joining.

questions.text: Before your first visit, what did you picture your time at the gym would be like?
questions.goal: To uncover the expectations members held before joining so they can be compared with reality.

questions.text: Can you walk me through what your first few weeks as a member were actually like?
questions.goal: To understand the early on-site experience, including onboarding, facilities, staff and atmosphere.

questions.text: How did going to the gym fit around the rest of your week, such as work, family or other commitments?
questions.goal: To learn about practical factors like time, location and routine that affected how often they went.

questions.text: When did you first start thinking about cancelling, and what was happening at that point?
questions.goal: To identify the moments, triggers and feelings that led to the decision to cancel.

questions.text: How would you describe the process of actually cancelling your membership?
questions.goal: To understand the cancellation experience and any friction or feelings it created.

questions.text: Looking back, what, if anything, could the gym have done differently during those first months?
questions.goal: To surface changes the gym could make that might have kept the member, without assuming any would have.

questions.text: How do you see yourself keeping active over the next year, and what role, if any, might a gym play in that?
questions.goal: To learn about future exercise plans and openness to rejoining a gym or choosing an alternative.

output.title: First Steps with a Banking App: Retirees' Experiences
output.audience: Retired people who have started, or tried to start, using a banking app on a smartphone for the first time
topics: How they managed their banking before the app
What led them to try a banking app
Setting up and first-time use
Help and support they used
Feelings about security and trust
Ongoing use and habits
Hopes for the future

questions.text: To start, could you tell me a bit about how you have usually looked after your banking over the years?
questions.goal: Understand their banking habits and routines before using an app, as context for the change.

questions.text: How did you first come to start using a banking app on your phone?
questions.goal: Learn what triggered the decision to try a banking app and who or what influenced it.

questions.text: Can you walk me through what happened the first time you tried to set up the app, step by step, as best you remember it?
questions.goal: Capture the real setup journey, including downloading, registering and logging in for the first time.

questions.text: Which parts of getting started, if any, took more time or effort than you expected, and what happened then?
questions.goal: Identify specific barriers and friction points in first-time use without assuming difficulty.

questions.text: Who or what, if anyone, did you turn to for help while getting started, and how did that go?
questions.goal: Understand the role of family, friends, bank staff, guides or other support in getting started.

questions.text: How do you feel about keeping your money and personal details safe when you use the app?
questions.goal: Explore attitudes to security and trust and how these shape their willingness to use the app.

questions.text: Thinking about the weeks after you first set it up, how has the way you use the app changed, if at all?
questions.goal: Learn how use develops over time, which features become habits and which are avoided.

questions.text: How does using the app compare with the other ways you have done your banking?
questions.goal: Understand how they weigh the app against branches, phone banking or other methods.

questions.text: If you could give advice to another retired person about to try a banking app for the first time, what would you tell them?
questions.goal: Surface the lessons and practical tips they consider most important from their own experience.

questions.text: Looking ahead, what would make banking on your phone work better for you in the future?
questions.goal: Gather forward-looking needs and ideas for improving the first-time and ongoing experience.

output.title: Refillable Cleaning Product Subscription: Renter Reactions
topics: Current cleaning product habits
Appeal of refills
Worries about subscriptions
Expected price
Storage space

questions.text: To start, could you walk me through how you usually get your household cleaning products, from noticing you're running low to having something new under the sink?
questions.goal: Understand current buying habits, including where, how often and how respondents shop for cleaning products.

questions.text: How do you decide which cleaning products or brands to buy?
questions.goal: Learn what drives current product and brand choices, such as price, scent, effectiveness or values.

questions.text: Imagine a service where you keep reusable bottles at home and get refills of cleaning products delivered. What are your first thoughts about that idea?
questions.goal: Capture unprompted initial reactions to the refill concept, both positive and negative.

questions.text: How, if at all, would switching to refills change the way you clean or shop compared with what you do now?
questions.goal: Explore the perceived appeal and drawbacks of refills relative to current habits.

questions.text: Thinking about subscriptions you have now or have had in the past, how have those experiences shaped how you feel about signing up for a new one?
questions.goal: Uncover past subscription experiences that influence openness or resistance to subscribing.

questions.text: What, if anything, would make you hesitate before signing up for a cleaning product subscription like this?
questions.goal: Identify specific worries about subscriptions, such as commitment, cancellation, delivery timing or unwanted products.

questions.text: How do you think about what a service like this should cost each month, and what would you compare it to?
questions.goal: Understand price expectations and the reference points respondents use to judge value.

questions.text: Tell me about where you keep cleaning supplies in your place right now and how that space works for you.
questions.goal: Learn about real storage constraints in rented city homes and how refill bottles and deliveries might fit.

questions.text: Looking ahead, what would a refill subscription need to look like for it to fit into your life over the next year or so?
questions.goal: Gather forward-looking requirements and conditions under which respondents might adopt the service.

output.title: Short Commutes: Choosing Between E-Scooter, Bus and Walking
output.audience: Commuters who regularly make trips under 3 km and who use, or could use, an e-scooter, the bus or walking for those trips
topics: Current short-trip habits and routines
How the choice between e-scooter, bus and walking is made
Practical factors such as time, cost, weather and distance
Perceptions of safety and comfort for each option
Barriers or hesitations around each option
Situations that change which option is used
Future intentions and what would change their choice

questions.text: Can you walk me through a typical short trip you make, under about 3 km, from the moment you decide to leave until you arrive?
questions.goal: To understand the respondent's real short-trip routine and context in their own words.

questions.text: When you have a short trip like that, how do you usually get there, and how did that become your usual way?
questions.goal: To learn their default mode and the history or habits behind it.

questions.text: Think about the last time you had to decide how to get somewhere close by. What went through your mind as you chose how to travel?
questions.goal: To uncover the actual decision process and which factors come to mind first.

questions.text: How would you describe the experience of getting around by e-scooter, by bus and on foot, based on what you've done or seen yourself?
questions.goal: To capture unprompted perceptions of each of the three options side by side.

questions.text: How, if at all, do things like weather, time of day or what you're carrying affect how you travel on short trips?
questions.goal: To identify situational factors that shift their choice from one option to another.

questions.text: How do you feel about safety and comfort when you think about each of these three ways of travelling?
questions.goal: To explore safety and comfort perceptions without assuming any option feels better or worse.

questions.text: What, if anything, makes you hesitate before using any of these options for a short trip?
questions.goal: To surface barriers such as cost, reliability, effort, access or rules for each option.

questions.text: Can you tell me about a time you travelled a short distance in a different way than you normally would? What led to that?
questions.goal: To find the triggers that cause people to switch modes in practice.

questions.text: Looking ahead, what would need to be different for you to change how you make your short trips?
questions.goal: To learn what changes in services, infrastructure or personal circumstances would shift future behaviour.

output.title: Why Coffee Drinkers Stopped Buying Pods
output.audience: Coffee drinkers who used to buy coffee pods but have stopped buying them
topics: Past experience with coffee pods
Reasons for stopping buying pods
The moment or trigger for the switch
What they use to make coffee now
How the current method compares with pods
What could bring them back to pods

questions.text: To start, could you tell me about your coffee habits on a typical day, from your first cup onwards?
questions.goal: Understand the respondent's current coffee routine and how central coffee is to their day.

questions.text: Thinking back to when you used coffee pods, how did they fit into your life back then?
questions.goal: Learn how and when pods were used, for how long, and what role they played in the routine.

questions.text: How would you describe your overall experience with coffee pods during the time you used them?
questions.goal: Capture the respondent's unprompted feelings about pods, both positive and negative, without suggesting either.

questions.text: Can you walk me through how you came to stop buying pods?
questions.goal: Uncover the sequence of events and any specific trigger or turning point that led to stopping.

questions.text: What were the main reasons behind your decision to stop buying pods?
questions.goal: Identify the underlying drivers of stopping, such as cost, taste, waste, convenience or machine issues, in the respondent's own words.

questions.text: How do you make or get your coffee now that you no longer use pods?
questions.goal: Find out which method, equipment, products or outlets have replaced pods.

questions.text: How did you go about choosing what you use now instead of pods?
questions.goal: Understand what options were considered and what influenced the choice of replacement.

questions.text: How does your current way of having coffee compare with using pods?
questions.goal: Learn what is better, worse or the same about the replacement relative to pods, as the respondent sees it.

questions.text: Looking ahead, what, if anything, would make you consider buying coffee pods again?
questions.goal: Identify the conditions or changes, if any, that could win the respondent back to pods.

output.title: Dog Owners' Views on Switching to Home-Delivered Fresh Dog Food
output.audience: Dog owners who decide what their dog eats, whatever they feed today, and who could switch to a home-delivered fresh dog food.
topics: Current feeding habits and how the food was chosen
Views on fresh dog food
Feelings about switching to a home-delivered fresh dog food
Cost and value
Trust in the ingredients
The vet's opinion and influence

questions.text: To start, tell me a bit about your dog and what a normal mealtime looks like for them.
questions.goal: Build rapport and understand the dog and the household's current feeding routine.

questions.text: How did you end up choosing the food your dog eats now?
questions.goal: Learn what drives current food choices and who or what shaped them.

questions.text: When you hear the words "fresh dog food", what comes to mind?
questions.goal: Uncover unprompted views of fresh dog food without assuming it is preferred.

questions.text: How would you feel about having your dog's food delivered to your door on a regular schedule?
questions.goal: Understand reactions to the home-delivery and subscription side of the offer, including practical pros and cons.

questions.text: How do you decide whether a dog food is worth what it costs?
questions.goal: Learn how owners judge cost and value, and what price-related trade-offs they make.

questions.text: What would you want to know about the ingredients in a dog food before you felt comfortable giving it to your dog?
questions.goal: Find out what builds or undermines trust in ingredients and what proof owners look for.

questions.text: What part, if any, does your vet play when you make decisions about your dog's food?
questions.goal: Gauge how much the vet's opinion influences food choices and how owners would involve the vet in a switch.

questions.text: What, if anything, would make you hesitate before switching your dog to a new food?
questions.goal: Identify barriers to switching, such as the dog's reaction, routine, cost or doubts, in the owner's own words.

questions.text: Thinking about the year ahead, how do you see the way you feed your dog changing, if at all?
questions.goal: Understand future intentions and openness to changing how they feed their dog.

output.title: Young Adults, Spending and Budgeting Apps
topics: How they keep track of their spending day to day
Tools and methods they use to track money
Experiences with budgeting apps
What makes them stop using budgeting apps
What would help them keep track of money in future

questions.text: To start off, tell me a bit about how money fits into your life right now, like where it comes from and what it usually goes on.
questions.goal: Understand the respondent's financial context, income sources and main spending areas as a warm-up.

questions.text: Walk me through how you keep an eye on what you spend in a typical week, if you do at all.
questions.goal: Learn their everyday habits and routines for tracking spending, including not tracking at all.

questions.text: What tools or methods, if any, have you used to keep track of your money, whether that's an app, a spreadsheet, notes, your banking app or something else?
questions.goal: Map the full range of tracking tools and methods they have tried, beyond dedicated budgeting apps.

questions.text: Think back to the first time you tried a budgeting app. What was going on in your life that made you try it?
questions.goal: Identify the triggers and motivations that lead young adults to start using a budgeting app.

questions.text: How would you describe your experience of using that app in the first few weeks?
questions.goal: Capture their unprompted early experience with a budgeting app, including any positives and frustrations.

questions.text: If you stopped using a budgeting app, tell me about what was happening around the time you stopped.
questions.goal: Uncover the specific moments, reasons and circumstances that lead them to give up on budgeting apps.

questions.text: How do you feel when you look closely at what you've been spending?
questions.goal: Explore the emotions tied to tracking spending and how those feelings may affect sticking with it.

questions.text: How do the people around you, like friends, family or partners, handle keeping track of their money, and how does that affect the way you do it?
questions.goal: Understand social influences on their tracking habits and attitudes toward budgeting.

questions.text: Looking ahead, what would need to be true for a way of tracking your money to become something you actually keep doing?
questions.goal: Identify the conditions, features or changes that would help them stick with tracking their spending in future.
